## Objective

Exercise the canonical and manual workflows plus two-project, rerun, conflict, and destination-boundary behavior in disposable environments.

## Scope

- Canonical route, manual route, two-project isolation, no-user-wide-log checks, version 1 path boundaries

## Entry conditions

- Both routes, root memory, and their focused tests are implemented and pass.

## Exit criteria

- TASK-025 through TASK-027 prove the complete user-relevant behavior without changing the live project registry or template state.

## Risks

- End-to-end fixtures can miss real path semantics or accidentally touch live state.
- Provider process-global state requires subprocess isolation.

### Risks

- Using the live Projects/ registry would create a real project and require separate cleanup authority.
- A fixture can be too weak if it does not preserve exact path and registry semantics.

### Acceptance criteria

- The fixture uses the exact production helper and a registered project-template entry under a workspace Projects/ container.
- One authorized run yields all required artifacts and checks with no transient template content, preview, duplicate, external path, or invented Git state.
- The live depot registry and Projects/ contents remain byte-identical except for separately tracked plan and Task records.

### Planned verification

- Run the canonical end-to-end test with the built wheel.
- Compare complete fixture and live workspace manifests before and after.
- Validate the initialization receipt and every adopted package.
- Exercise the installed console executable with no injected dispatcher; assert copied content has no Git identity and per-project status reporting rejects parent-root inheritance.

### Risks

- Manual steps could omit registry or asset verification and appear equivalent only at the memory layer.
- The test must never initialize the template itself.

### Acceptance criteria

- The manually copied and specialized project reaches the same identity, asset, configuration, isolation, runtime, and receipt contract after one direct init-memory invocation.
- The template remains byte-identical and uninitialized.
- Differences limited to entry-route authorization and sequencing are documented; no executable bootstrap logic is duplicated.
- The manual project receives exactly the reviewed depot baseline skills/soul and a factual nonduplicate registry entry through shared preparation; stale template packages cannot silently remain the active baseline.

### Planned verification

- Execute the documented manual route in a disposable fixture.
- Compare canonical and manual artifact manifests and verification outcomes.
- Reinspect the template for any derived state.

### Risks

- Process-global Cognee state can make in-process tests pass or fail for the wrong reason.
- Failure cases must not leave transaction-owned artifacts in the live workspace.

### Acceptance criteria

- Each project returns only its own records and relations and uses its own data, system, cache, log, model, index, receipt, and dataset paths.
- All forbidden destination and conflict cases fail before mutation, while an equivalent rerun is non-duplicating.
- Subprocess and filesystem evidence shows no new ~/.cognee/log or other account-wide state.

### Planned verification

- Run isolated subprocess tests for both projects.
- Compare provider, exact-index, cache, log, and receipt manifests.
- Run all destination and rerun cases and inspect rejected-case state.
